subject: Clarify uptime coverage for 2026-12-08 maintenance + CDN degradation
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@northbay.health>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 08 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Uptime calculation dispute for 2026-12-08 window

Hi Karthik,

Quick note from our Ops team — between 03:50 and 04:34 UTC on 2026-12-08 we saw sustained 5xx errors and elevated latency hitting our production inference endpoints. Our monitoring shows a ~25% request error rate for that 44-minute period which we believe should be counted against Redwood's SLA window.

However, when we reviewed the first pass of your uptime report (attached) the outage seems to have been excluded because of a Redwood-scheduled maintenance window that started at 03:45 UTC. From our side, the majority of failed requests occurred after 03:50, and critical traffic was impacted despite the stated maintenance. We need clarification on two points:

- How are partial degradations during a scheduled maintenance window attributed in your uptime calc?
- If third-party CDN failures contributed (we saw edge timeouts), how does Redwood apportion responsibility between Redwood-scheduled maintenance and third-party provider impact?

We are preparing an audit packet and would like formal confirmation whether this event will be treated as "maintenance-excluded" for SLA purposes. This affects our December invoice and the renewal discussion tied to NB-4821.

I've attached our local request traces and a small CSV excerpt of error counts. Happy to hop on a short call with SREs if that helps.

Thanks,
Samir
Director, Platform Reliability
NorthBay Health

Attachments:
- uptime_report_NB-4821.csv (csv)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@northbay.health>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 08 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Uptime calculation dispute for 2026-12-08 window

Hi Samir — thanks for the heads up and for the traces. We take these reports seriously and want to get this squarely resolved.

High level next steps:
1) I'll loop in our SRE (Marissa) to reconcile our incident timeline and the Redis/CDN traces you sent.
2) Please send the HubSpot ticket or Drive link you referenced so we can attach the artifacts to NB-4821 (we have the preliminary report but we'll need your full trace set for cross-correlation).
3) If the impact falls outside what our maintenance scope covers or is attributable to a Redwood runtime regression, we'll propose an SLA adjustment or one-time concession.

For transparency, Redwood's maintenance windows are typically described in the customer config and may exclude events that are strictly within a defined maintenance period. That said, partial degradations that persist after the maintenance end or that are caused by outbound third-party dependency failures are often handled differently — Marissa will share the exact policy excerpt and our timeline.

I'm available for a 30-minute call tomorrow (Wed) between 15:00-17:00 UTC if that works for you and Jane.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

> Quick note from our Ops team — between 03:50 and 04:34 UTC on 2026-12-08 we saw sustained 5xx errors...
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@northbay.health>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 09 Dec 2026 15:27:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Uptime calculation dispute for 2026-12-08 window

Samir — I pulled the raw runtime logs and correlated them with our scheduled maintenance and CDN provider telemetry. Summary below (high level):

- Scheduled maintenance: 03:45:00 - 03:55:00 UTC (configuration push to dedicated pool nodes). This was a planned maintenance window announced in the tenant config for NB-4821.
- Observed degradation: Starts ~03:50:30 UTC, peaks 03:58 - 04:10 UTC, tailing off by 04:34 UTC. Error types: 502/504 and increased tail latency for token generation.
- Third-party impact: Our edge CDN showed elevated connection handshakes between 03:52 and 04:05 UTC with increased timeouts reported to our control plane. We capture these as external dependency events.

Why this is tricky: your failed requests cluster both inside and after the maintenance window. Redwood's current SLA calculation logic does two things: it excludes the portion of downtime strictly labeled as "scheduled maintenance" in the tenant's maintenance calendar, but it does count any residual errors that persist after the maintenance end if the runtime is still returning 5xx for customer requests. If a third-party CDN caused the majority of failures and it is independently classified, we may attribute the outage to that provider, which can change entitlement for Redwood credit depending on whether the provider is a covered dependency in your contract.

Preliminary reconciliation (attached logs):
- redwood_incident_log_2026-12-08.txt: our per-node request logs and ingress latency.
- uptime_report_NB-4821.csv: preliminary uptime calc with time buckets.

Our proposal for moving forward:
1) We suggest a hybrid attribution: exclude the strictly scheduled maintenance window (03:45-03:55 UTC), and then apportion the residual 03:55-04:34 UTC period between Redwood runtime and CDN depending on trace-level error signatures. I've highlighted the buckets where our traces show backend 5xx vs edge-level timeouts.
2) If NorthBay's contract (NB-4821) designates the CDN as a Redwood-managed dependency, Redwood would cover the full residual window; if the CDN is customer-managed, we would treat it as a third-party incident and exclude that portion from Redwood SLA credits.
3) To be proactive, Redwood is prepared to offer a one-time goodwill billing adjustment for the residual 03:58-04:10 UTC high-impact tail while we finish the full cross-correlation. This is outside of formal SLA credit calculation but aims to mitigate immediate billing concerns while we finalize investigation.

Please confirm receipt of the attached logs and tell us whether your team manages the CDN configuration (we ask because that changes the attribution model). Happy to set the call Karthik suggested — I can bring our runtime engineer.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Attachments:
- redwood_incident_log_2026-12-08.txt (text)
- uptime_report_NB-4821.csv (csv)

Cc: Jane Liu <jane.liu@northbay.health>
Date: Thu, 11 Dec 2026 16:30:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Uptime calculation dispute for 2026-12-08 window

Karthik / Marissa — thanks for the quick turnaround and for sharing the reconciliation. We received the attachments and have reviewed the hybrid attribution proposal. A few points from our side:

- The CDN for NB-4821 is managed by a third-party (we have a separate contract with EdgeFast). Per our procurement terms, we expect Redwood to disclose which dependencies are considered in-scope for SLA coverage; that was not explicit in the renewal paperwork.
- We appreciate the one-time goodwill adjustment offer. Procurement has asked for formal confirmation in writing (amount/credit method) so we can close our December invoice and proceed with the renewal conversation for next quarter.

Next steps requested:
1) Please provide a written statement that specifies which timestamps Redwood will exclude from SLA calculations and which will be attributed to third-party CDN (preferably in CSV time-bucket form).
2) If Redwood proceeds with a goodwill billing adjustment, provide the credit amount or % and confirm it will be reflected on the December invoice or as a separate credit memo.
3) Include the HubSpot ticket link (NB-4821) and any internal SR/incident id so our procurement and accounting teams can reconcile.

We can go to a short exec call if that helps, but procurement prefers to have the written artifacts first.

Thanks,
Samir
Director, Platform Reliability
NorthBay Health
